title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
layout_note: One grey 'Atlas' box in the centre; example task inputs on the left and their outputs on the right connect to it by curved arrows; below the hub a stack of three grey retrieved-passage cards is fetched and returned by a curved arrow loop; a dashed horizontal rule splits a Pretraining row from a Few-shot row.
grouping: A horizontal dashed rule with monospace labels 'Pretraining' (above) and 'Few-shot' (below) splits the figure into two rows; each task is a colour family shared between its input box (left) and output box (right): green = masked language modelling, yellow = fact checking, orange = question answering.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with dark outlines and pastel fills; the hub is a large grey box with the name in big bold monospace; retrieved passages are three overlapping grey cards, offset diagonally to read as a stack, holding centred italic text.
proposed_highlight: The model is the single large grey hub named in heavy monospace type; everything else (tasks, retrieved passage) radiates from it with curved arrows.
lesson: Show one model serving several tasks by putting it as a central hub with colour-matched input and output boxes on either side, and draw retrieval as a stack of text cards below the hub with an out-and-back curved arrow.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; remembered venue JMLR 2023 (not printed on the first page of this arXiv version). Chosen as the method figure because the paper has no architecture diagram (Fig. 2 is task examples, Figs. 3-4 are in the appendix). It shows the model as one black-box hub, not its retriever/reader internals.

arrangement.units: Two horizontal lanes separated by a dashed rule: the top lane holds the pretraining (masked LM) input and output, the bottom lane the few-shot tasks; the central Atlas hub and the retrieved-passage stack straddle both lanes with no frame.
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted example sentences in italic inside pastel boxes, each headed by a bold underlined task name
arrangement.shared: the single Atlas hub and one retrieved-passage stack are drawn once and serve every task's arrows

taxonomy.task: few-shot knowledge-intensive tasks (fact checking, question answering) with a retrieval-augmented LM

core.what: one central grey 'Atlas' hub serving every task: colour-matched input boxes on the left and output boxes on the right connect to it by curved arrows, the same hub for pretraining and few-shot tasks

relations.form: three task-input boxes on the left (masked LM, fact checking, question answering) converge by curved arrows on the hub's left edge, and three matching outputs fan out from its right edge

a stack of three grey passage cards below the hub, the top one quoting a real retrieved passage, fetched by a curved arrow from the hub's lower left and returned by a curved arrow up into its lower right

each input box and its output box share a pastel fill and sit on the same row across the hub (green MLM -> 'western part', yellow fact -> 'False', peach QA -> 'Western part of the North Atlantic Ocean')
a dashed horizontal rule splits the top Pretraining row from the Few-shot rows below, both rows using the same hub

channels.colour: pastel fill = task, matched between each input and its output (green, yellow, peach); grey = Atlas and its retrieved passages
channels.shape: rounded boxes with a bold underlined task name over an italic quoted sentence = task examples; stacked cards = retrieved documents; one large box = the model
channels.line: solid curved arrows for all flow; dashed rule = training phase boundary
channels.frame: no containers; the dashed rule partitions phases

quality.strengths: data drawn as data - every input, output and retrieved passage is a real quoted sentence about the same Bermuda Triangle fact, so the reader follows one example through every task; colour has one meaning (task), matched across the hub; retrieval drawn as a document stack beside the main flow with an out-and-back arrow
quality.weaknesses: the model is a blank labelled box, so nothing shows how the retrieved passages are combined with the query; curved arrows bundle into the hub's corners and cross the dashed phase rule; the hub and passages share grey, so retrieved data and model look the same kind of thing

insights.structure: A single grey Atlas hub sits in the centre with task inputs stacked on the left, matching outputs stacked on the right, and a stack of retrieved-passage cards directly below it.
insights.data: Inputs, outputs and the retrieved passage are all real sentences about one shared example (the Bermuda Triangle), italic in pastel boxes, so the retrieved text visibly contains the answers.
insights.emphasis: The model name is the largest text in the figure, in bold monospace on the biggest box, and the same example threads through every task.
insights.flow: Curved arrows converge from the left boxes into the hub, curve down to the passage stack and back up, then fan out to the right boxes.
insights.avoid: The model is a black box, so the figure shows what Atlas does but not how retriever and language model connect; do not use this pattern when the architecture is the contribution.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
